answers.question: What range of flow speeds did the BASS-II wind tunnel cover?
answers.answer:
From the evidence ledger (values as reported, no conversion):
- BASS-II poster: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (BASS-II wind tunnel); various solid samples; microgravity (ISS); 21% and below; flow up to 40 cm/s: maximum airflow speed of wind tunnel = 40 cm/s (upper bound) [R090]
- BASS-II poster: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (BASS-II); PMMA sheet; microgravity (ISS); flow varied: flow speed below which radiative quenching occurs = 2 cm/s (upper bound) [R082]
- BASS-II poster: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (BASS-II); PMMA sheet; microgravity (ISS); flow varied: flow speed near blow-off extinction = 40 cm/s (approximate) [R083]
- BASS-II poster: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (BASS-II); SIBAL fabric; microgravity (ISS); 1 atm; 18.7%; flow 5 cm/s at ignition: flow speed after gradual reduction (quenching sequence) = 2.2 cm/s [R089]
- BASS-II poster: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (BASS-II); various solid samples; microgravity (ISS); 21% and below; flow 0 to 55 cm/s: airflow speed range = 0 to 55 cm/s (range) [R091]

answers.question: Which materials have been burned in lunar gravity, and on which platforms?
answers.answer:
Matching tests in the ledger:
- FM2 poster: lunar-gravity centrifuge and parabolic flight; SIBAL fabric (cotton/fiberglass blend); lunar (simulated); air [R076]
- Feier et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; thin cellulose (Kimwipes); 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 G; 0.2-0.4 atm; 21% O2, balance N2 [R098]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; SIBAL fabric and PMMA rod (burned simultaneously); lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air [R026]
- Sacksteder et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; Kimwipes thin cellulosic tissue; partial gravity (0.1, 0.16, 0.38 g); 27.6 kPa; air [R092]
- Sacksteder et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; Kimwipes thin cellulosic tissue; partial gravity (0.1, 0.16, 0.38 g); 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia); air [R093]
- FM2 poster: FM2 on a lunar lander (planned); PMMA (acrylic) rod; lunar (on the Moon); 8.2 psia; 34%; planned, no result yet [R073] [R075]

answers.question: How did LUCI's lunar-gravity flame spread rates compare with its 1 g burns?
answers.answer:

- LUCI: ground, LUCI 1-g burns; SIBAL fabric (cotton-fiberglass); 1 g; ~20% (roughly constant): flame tip spread rate = 2.8 mm/s [R004]
- LUCI: ground, LUCI 1-g burns; PMMA (acrylic) rod; 1 g; 21% at start, falling to 14.5%: flame tip spread rate = 0.40 cm/s [R008]
- LUCI: ground, LUCI 1-g burns; PMMA (acrylic) rod; 1 g; 21% at start, falling to 14.5%: flame tip growth rate at start of burn = 3.95 mm/s (approximate) [R011]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; SIBAL fabric (cotton-fiberglass); lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: flame base spread rate = 0.92 mm/s [R001]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; SIBAL fabric (cotton-fiberglass); lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: flame tip spread rate = 1.1 mm/s [R002]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; PMMA (acrylic) rod; lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: flame tip spread rate = 0.15 cm/s [R007]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; PMMA (acrylic) rod; lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: peak instantaneous flame base spread rate (before 125 s) = 0.6 mm/s (approximate) [R022]
